# Right Time, Right Place

Version 1.4.0 gives every feed date a time-zone-aware companion, keeps your last feed on screen when a poll fails, and tightens how links and local files are handled.

## Dates with a time zone

- **Every date now has an ISO 8601 companion.** Dates left the integration only as text in your `date_format`, and the default format has no time zone, so a card had to guess. `published`, `updated`, `created` and `expired`, in entries and in `channel`, now come with `published_iso` and so on, for example `2026-11-13T19:12:37+00:00`. The formatted value and `date_format` stay as they were. The companion follows its source key through `inclusions`, can be dropped on its own through `exclusions`, and is never shortened by `max_text_length`.
- **rss-accordion uses the new fields.** The card now prefers the `_iso` values, so times are correct across time zones and a custom format such as `%d.%m.%Y` no longer breaks them. It still works with feeds from before this version.

## A feed that survives a failed poll

- **The sensor keeps the last feed when a poll fails.** Before, a failed poll made the sensor unavailable and the whole `entries` list vanished from cards. Now the sensor stays available, keeps the last good feed and sets `stale: true` until the next poll succeeds. A feed that never loaded is still unavailable. If an automation uses `unavailable` as an outage signal, use the `stale` attribute instead.

## Links and local files

- **Relative links in the text are resolved too.** Relative `href` and `src` values in the summary, content and subtitle HTML used to point at your Home Assistant host. They are now joined with the feed URL, as `link` and `links[].href` are. URLs such as `javascript:` are still removed.
- **Relative entry links are resolved.** A relative `link` or `links[].href` is now joined with the feed URL even when the feed library supplies it.
- **`file://` feeds are limited to allowed folders.** Before, any file the Home Assistant user could read could be used as a feed. Now only the config directory and folders in `allowlist_external_dirs` work. Anything else is refused with an error that says how to allow the folder. The README lists which `file://` feeds are allowed.

## Smaller history, quieter log

- **Entries and channel stay out of the recorder.** They were written to the history on every change. They are now left out, so the database stays small. The live state is unchanged and `feed_url` is still recorded.
- **The size warning measures what is recorded.** It claimed the history would lose its attributes even for verbose feeds. It now only appears for an absurdly long feed URL, and says so.
- **Repeated problems are logged once.** "No entries found" and "Unable to parse date" were warnings on every poll. The first occurrence per feed is still a warning, repeats go to debug.

## Fixes and upkeep

- **README corrections.** The example used `description` under `inclusions` where the key is `summary`, the `date_format` default was missing `%Y`, and `scan_interval` is a time period with a default of one hour, not hours.
- **Marketplace category.** The integration is now filed under news and social media in Home Assistant 2026.11's Marketplace.
- **Home Assistant 2026.11 typing.** The device info is built in a way that works on both older and newer Home Assistant.

## Requirements

Unchanged: Home Assistant 2026.9.3 or newer.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do after updating. New `_iso` attributes appear on the next poll. If you read local `file://` feeds from outside the config directory, add that folder to `allowlist_external_dirs`. If an automation treats `unavailable` as a failed poll, switch it to the `stale` attribute.
